**Renaming a project does not fix its refs, and that is deliberate. Recording it so nobody tries it twice.**

Hit today: a new project *Peek's Intelligence* produced `PEE-1`…`PEE-6`, colliding with *Peek: Feedback & Bugs*, which produces the same prefix. Renaming it to **Intelligence in Peek** changed the project title and **left all six issues on `PEE-`**.

A renamed project therefore ends up holding `PEE-1…6` followed by `INT-1…`, which is worse than either consistent option. Review feedback corrected my scope call, and the existing code argued for it better than I did. Peek decided open-vs-done with a hardcoded English word set matched on lowercased labels, and **its own comment admitted** *"an app whose statuses are spelled differently shows an empty section until its values are added here — the failure worth having"*. For a layer whose purpose is making the third app cheap, that is PEE-10: blank reads as "that app is broken".

So the owning app declares it: `stage: open | started | done | dropped`.

**`dropped` is the one that earns its place.** A cancelled ticket is neither open nor done — counted as open a finished project sits at 3/4 for ever; counted as done it claims abandoned work. Only the owner knows which statuses have that shape.

**The boundary:** stage says what a status means, never what to draw. "1/3" vs a progress bar vs nothing stays the consumer's call — an owner that could set that would be designing another app's UI, which is §13.1's iframe objection. Declaring meaning is the inversion working; declaring layout would be it breaking.
